name: Web
description: Fetch pages as readable text. No key, no account, nothing to pay for.
long_description:
Reads a page the way a reader mode does: navigation, cookie banners, share rails and comment threads are stripped, and what comes back is the article, its title and the address it ended up at after redirects.

A page too long for one reply is not cut off: it comes back a window at a time, and the model reads on from where it stopped without fetching it again.

Only http and https, and only the public internet. Anything that resolves to this machine or to your own network — a router's admin page, a database on localhost, a cloud metadata service — is refused, and the check runs again on every redirect, so a public address cannot bounce the fetch inward. No cookies are sent or kept, so a page is fetched as a stranger sees it and never as you.

This connector is free and stays free. It asks for no key, keeps no account, and has no quota you can exhaust or buy your way out of. Searching the web is not built yet; when it is, it will be keyless too.

Where the chat's model has web search of its own, that is used for finding pages. This is the tool for reading them.

risk.notes: Reads pages from the public internet and nothing on this machine. Private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused, on the first request and on every redirect. No cookies are sent or stored, and no credentials of any kind are asked for or held.

prompt.system_addendum: Prefer fetch_url over guessing at a page's contents from its URL. A page's text is what it says now; quote it rather than recalling it. A long page arrives one window at a time: when a result says more, call fetch_url again with the next_offset it gives you rather than answering from the first part alone. Reading on is free — the page is already in memory and is not fetched twice.
